episode_title: Serious Cocktails, Seriously Fun Hospitality with Brian Evans

real_qa.q: How did Brian Evans transition from wine and sommelier work to becoming a cocktail-focused bartender at Sunday Hospitality Group?
real_qa.r: Evans initially pursued a career as a sommelier or wine buyer after working with lower ABV wine, sake, and beer programs in Austin for six years. After moving to New York City to chase mentors from the city, he was thrown behind the bar within his first three months and became hyper-obsessed with cocktails and classics. A turning point came when he worked part-time at Michelin-starred restaurant Betony in 2015, where he learned high-wire mixology and flavor extraction techniques from bartender Eamon Rocky, which completely changed his perspective on drinks making.
real_qa.requete: Brian Evans bartender career Sunday Hospitality Group

real_qa.q: What is the bar training program structure that Sunday Hospitality Group uses when opening new venues?
real_qa.r: Sunday Hospitality Group uses an intensive training program for each bar opening, starting day one with introducing bar tools and their proper usage including how to shake and stir. The training covers classic cocktails, proper technique for egg white cocktails, order of operation by measuring cheapest or smallest ingredients first moving to most expensive. Brian Evans works with bar operations manager Cassandra Lee, described as highly organized and knowledgeable about the scientific process of flavor work, to ensure consistent training across all venues.
real_qa.requete: Sunday Hospitality Group bar training program

real_qa.q: How does Sunday Hospitality Group balance global flavors and multicultural cocktail approaches with guest familiarity and comfort?
real_qa.r: Evans emphasizes that menu verbiage is very important and keeping descriptions short and sweet, aiming to undersell and over deliver. He uses one intriguing word in ingredient lists to stimulate engagement, and avoids correcting guests on pronunciation unless asked. Cocktail menus list only the name with no more than four to five words following, leaving brand names off, which creates table talk opportunities for staff to engage guests and explain cultural concepts like a bamboo cocktail that originated in San Francisco but became a smash success in Japan.
real_qa.requete: global flavors cocktails menu cultural approach

real_qa.q: What was Brian Evans' experience opening the first Sunday Hospitality Group bar concepts at The Hoxton in Los Angeles compared to New York?
real_qa.r: Evans' first opening from scratch was the dual LA concepts within The Hoxton Hotel in 2019, which was a major learning curve as he had never bartended in California or Los Angeles. He found the LA bartending community exhilarating with different approaches to speakeasies and excellent hospitality, but experienced less burnout in personalities compared to New York. His main takeaway was that LA's large bar spaces sometimes negatively affected vibe on slower nights, but the interior design of many spaces was captivating and the team he hired and trained was super stoked to improve their cocktail game.
real_qa.requete: Sunday Hospitality Group Hoxton Los Angeles opening

real_qa.q: How does Sunday Hospitality Group maintain fun and experiential elements in cocktail service while preserving professionalism?
real_qa.r: Evans explains that Sunday prioritizes making sure guests have fun while maintaining professionalism through techniques like setting drinks on fire, delivering martinis in ice-encased bottles, and honoring historical New York moments with oversized menus. He notes that fun needs to be delivered in a way that is not silly, and the group ensures staff equips themselves with storytelling elements that prove a cocktail's relevance on the menu, allowing servers and bartenders to engage guests without schooling them.

guest.bio_context: Brian Evans started his hospitality career at coffee shops in Fort Smith, Arkansas, then moved to Austin, Texas where he initially pursued wine and sommelier careers before being drawn to cocktails. After six years in Austin, he moved to New York City to study under mentors from the city, and within three months of arriving was thrown behind the bar where he became obsessed with cocktail classics and spirits. He worked part-time at Michelin-starred restaurant Betony in 2015, where he learned high-wire mixology from bartender Eamon Rocky, and later joined Sunday Hospitality Group as a part-time bartender at Sunday in Brooklyn before being promoted to head bartender and eventually Director of Bars overseeing multiple venues.
